# Marginal decision framework

Compare the change in benefits and costs between feasible alternatives. A past expense that cannot be recovered does not change with the new decision and is sunk. A new avoidable campaign expense belongs in the launch comparison. Unit contribution is selling price less variable cost; fixed incremental campaign cost is then deducted from total contribution. Opportunity costs can matter even when no accounting payment is made, but the analyst needs evidence rather than inventing their magnitude.

Treat forecast volume as a scenario, not an observation. A positive scenario contribution is not automatically a risk-free decision or complete after-tax valuation. Capacity constrains feasibility. When cannibalization, working-capital, tax or opportunity-value evidence is missing, retain those gaps rather than assuming no effect. Break-even analysis can make the demand uncertainty concrete without claiming the forecast has been validated.

## Preparation questions

1. Which expenses enter the incremental launch decision?
2. Why is a forecast not evidence of confirmed orders?
3. What information is needed before calling the launch risk-free?
